items.headline: Semiconductor index falls eight straight sessions, about 24% below its June peak
items.why: Roughly $1 trillion of value left chip stocks while the big AI spenders fell only about 1%, so the market is punishing the suppliers whose revenue depends on someone else's financing.

items.headline: CoreWeave 2032 bonds drop to about 78 cents; credit swaps imply over 60% five-year default odds
items.why: It is the first visible credit stress in the AI data-center build-out, and one analyst estimate has about $10B of operating cash flow set against roughly $45B of capex over the next year.

items.headline: TSMC Q3 revenue $46.72B (+16.2% quarter on quarter, 66.4% gross margin); ASML lifts full-year sales guidance to EUR 44-45B
items.why: Order and revenue data from the two key chip suppliers remain strong, so the sell-off is about how AI spending gets funded, not about demand disappearing.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin and ether ETFs shed about $548M in the week to Oct 16; ether funds log a third straight weekly outflow
items.why: Ether funds have now lost roughly $1B over three weeks, a sign institutional demand is fading even as prices hold up.

sources.title: Ethereum ETFs lose more money than Bitcoin ETFs last week

items.headline: Bitcoin holds near $82K after hot CPI and PPI; ether near $2,440; bitcoin is still about 26% lower year on year
items.why: Crypto did not sell off on an inflation surprise that hit stocks and bonds, but it remains well below its 2025 highs, so resilience is not yet a trend.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Friday, October 16, 2026

items.headline: About $106M of leveraged ether longs liquidated within an hour of the CPI release
items.why: Leverage is concentrated on the long side of ether, so a surprise data print can force selling that has nothing to do with spot demand.

sources.title: Ethereum ETFs lose more money than Bitcoin ETFs last week

items.headline: September CPI hits 3.7% year on year (3.6% expected), +0.6% on the month; PPI up 1.3% on the month
items.why: Gasoline drove more than half the monthly CPI rise, and a producer-price jump this large means energy costs are feeding into the wider economy.

items.headline: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the Sept 16 hike; markets put only 10-16% odds on an Oct 27-28 hike but about 89% on December
items.why: The next move is priced as up, so any soft data or an oil drop is what would change the path, not the October meeting itself.

sources.title: Gold Price Week Ahead: Bull and Bear Case From $4,166

items.headline: Renewed attacks near the Strait of Hormuz push Brent to about $110; the IEA speeds up emergency reserve releases
items.why: Even a larger release, including over 20M barrels of diesel, failed to calm prices, which tells you the supply fear is about flow through the Gulf, not stock levels.

items.headline: IMF flags rising government bond yields as the main financial-stability threat; French spread over Germany widens to about 139 bp
items.why: Global yields near 4.5% are at an 18-year high, and wider spreads in France show markets starting to charge for fiscal risk.

items.headline: Brent up 6.6% on the week to $109.68 and WTI up 12.0% to $101.89
items.why: WTI gained far more than Brent and the gap narrowed from about $12 to under $8, a sign US crude is being pulled hard into export demand.

items.headline: Gold slips 0.7% to about $4,166 while silver drops 6.3% to about $57
items.why: Gold is holding near $4,200 despite a surging oil price and hot inflation, but silver's much larger drop shows the industrial side of metals is weakening.

items.headline: Lithium carbonate falls 16.5% to CNY 102,150 a tonne; copper down 2.2% to about $6.52 a pound
items.why: Lithium was the biggest weekly mover of nine commodities tracked, and weak copper alongside it points to softer industrial and battery demand expectations.

items.headline: US distillate stocks at their lowest seasonal level on record; pump diesel and gasoline average about $6.17 a gallon
items.why: Thin diesel inventories into winter leave little buffer, which is why the diesel releases matter more than the headline crude number.

items.headline: S&P 500 down about 2.0% on the week, its worst since June; Nasdaq Composite down about 4.5%; equal-weight S&P and Dow both up
items.why: Losses were confined to mega-cap AI and chip names while the average stock gained, so this looks like a leadership break rather than a broad market break.

sources.title: Stocks on Pace for Weekly Loss Despite Yield Drop

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield falls from about 5.33% to 5.05% in roughly 24 hours, the sharpest drop since June, then steadies near 5.1%
items.why: The pullback from a multi-year high is what let non-tech stocks rise this week, and a move back above 5.3% would put that support at risk.

sources.title: Stocks on Pace for Weekly Loss Despite Yield Drop

items.headline: Gold sits in a $4,100-$4,240 range, with $4,330 above and $3,970 below as the levels to watch; record is $5,597
items.why: Gold is still about 25% under its January high, so a close outside this range is the signal that the next leg has started.

sources.title: Gold Price Week Ahead: Bull and Bear Case From $4,166

items.headline: Fear & Greed index drops to 18 (extreme fear) from 45; money-market funds take in $166.4B, the most since April 2020
items.why: Extreme-fear readings with record cash moving to the sidelines have often marked short-term lows, but the index alone is not a buy signal.
